rankability.floor_basis: declared, not derived: no published source states a distinct-share floor. The reasoning is that at half the scores duplicated, half of any top N is placed by the tie-break rather than by the model, which argues for a floor near the middle of the range and does not single out this value over 0.45 or 0.55. Read a verdict near the floor as near a convention

largest_tie.reads_as: a handful of molecules on the most common score is many small collisions: the scores are not fine enough to separate neighbours. Most of the set on one score would be the opposite -- the model not distinguishing them at all -- and would be answered by different data rather than by a different specification

rankability.not_comparable: this share moves with the number measured, so it does not compare with another specification's unless both were measured on the same count
rankability.means: a top N cannot be drawn from this set: 46.8% of scores are distinct against a 50% floor declared before the run, measured on 1,200 molecules, so whatever breaks the tie would be choosing them rather than the score. this counts molecules that score the same, which is not the same as molecules the model cannot tell apart: the score is a sum over the fingerprint bits, so anything the fingerprint maps to one pattern scores identically whatever the model has learned. What is tied here is measured under 'what to measure'.

applicability.threshold_source: nearest-neighbour Tanimoto cut-offs of 0.4 to 0.6 are common applicability-domain practice; 0.4 is the lenient end of that band

control.test: hold 300 rows out of IMI-COMBINE and measure each one's greatest Tanimoto to the remaining 21,752
control.expected: high, because the molecules come from the same collection
control.what_it_rules_out: a fingerprint radius or bit-length mismatch, or salts and stereochemistry left on one side. Any of those would depress the control too.

applicability.means: 99.9% of this set sits outside the structures the model was fitted on, while 0.1% reaches the threshold (median 0.214, max 0.457 against a 0.4 threshold). An order can be produced; its meaning is not established.

activity_model.means: the gram-positive label, used as a stand-in for target binding without the permeability barrier
activity_model.note: IMI-COMBINE carries four organism classes (gram-negative, gram-positive, fungi, acid-fast) with pMIC values. Which one to fit on is a decision, not a default.

activity prediction.problem: the set sits outside the structures the model was fitted on

measured_alternatives.tie_note: IMI-COMBINE and B3DB are level within the precision these medians are reported to; neither is nearer

measured_alternatives.caveat: no primary amine in 1,132 rows (measured 2026-10-14). A specification requiring one has no near neighbour here by construction, which is why the nearest-set comparison puts it far

activity prediction.what_this_means: the training set listed first is the one this library is actually nearest to. If none reaches the threshold, no model fitted on what is here can speak about this library, and the revision is data rather than a setting.

ranking.problem: only 46.8% of scores are distinct against a 50% floor, so a top N would be the tie-break's

measured_alternatives.why_this_bounds_the_score_count: the score is a sum of the weights of the bits that are on, so two molecules with the same fingerprint get the same score exactly. The distinct scores cannot outnumber the distinct fingerprints, and may fall below them where different fingerprints happen to sum alike

ruled_out.reads_as: the same count at a larger radius or more bits means the collisions are not hash crowding: the molecules are identical to what a fingerprint looks at

what_the_duplicates_are.reads_as: a group that collapses to one structure when stereochemistry is dropped is a set of isomers the library carries separately and the fingerprint does not distinguish

what_would_separate_them.what_it_would_take: the activity model is fitted on fingerprints that ignore chirality, so scoring with one that does not would score in a space the model never saw. It is a refit, not a flag
what_would_separate_them.and_it_is_a_chemical_decision: whether two stereoisomers should be ranked apart depends on the target, which this tool does not know. That the library lists them separately is not the same question

measured_alternatives.what_does_not_help: a looser specification. Every specification selects from the same molecules, and the ones sharing a fingerprint share it under all of them

ranking.short_by: 38 more distinct scores would reach the floor, out of 1,200 measured. The percentage alone does not say whether that is a near miss or a different order of magnitude
ranking.what_this_means: the set can still be screened; what cannot be done is to take the top N from it, because the molecules at the top share a score and something other than the score would be picking between them

note: this module answers what a screen would establish. It does not return molecules; choosing which to make is the researcher's.
